subject: HIPAA discovery: BAA availability, PHI handling, deployment qualification
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@mediflow.io>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@mediflow.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from today’s HIPAA discovery call

Hi Diane / Samir —

Great to speak with you this morning. Quick recap from our call and the recommended next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve kept the asks focused so your security and engineering teams can triage efficiently.

Recap (what we covered)
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I and is targeting SOC 2 Type II in Q3 2026; we can provide the SOC 2 Type I report and an evidence index today.
- BAA: Redwood is able to execute a Business Associate Agreement. Our standard BAA covers Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private deployments (VPC/on‑prem). Hosted API (public multi‑tenant) is limited to de‑identified data and is not covered under the standard BAA.
- PHI handling boundaries: PHI may be processed on Dedicated and Private modes only. For Hosted API we recommend de‑identification or you can route traffic through a Private deployment for PHI workloads. Keys and logs: customer KMS integration (bring-your-own) is supported in Private; Dedicated supports customer-managed keys with a managed option.
- Data residency & weights: Model weights remain in Redwood-managed compute; customer data paths are constrained by the deployment mode (Private keeps data within your VPC).

Requested next steps (we can action within 3 business days):
1) I’ve attached the initial vendor security questionnaire (vendor_security_questionnaire_Mediflow.pdf). Please send back with priority items flagged.
2) We’ve attached a draft BAA (redwood_baa_draft_20260714.pdf) for your legal team to review.
3) Ben will assemble a short compliance packet (SOC evidence index + network diagrams). Expect a link from him by EOD.
4) Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical call to confirm key exchange, logging retention, and routing by Thursday 2026-07-16 at 10:00 AM PT — is that workable?

Open items for your team to confirm:
- Expected throughput and peak tokens per second for PHI flows (helps size Dedicated pool).
- Which environments do you plan to run PHI in (prod only, or prod + staging)?
- Any additional regulatory constraints (state-level requirements, Canadian PIPEDA, EU requirements)?

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_Mediflow.pdf (fillable), redwood_baa_draft_20260714.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415‑555‑0188

From: Diane Park <diane.park@mediflow.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@mediflow.io>
Date: 2026-07-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today’s HIPAA discovery call

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop legal:
1) Token logging retention: what is the default retention for request/response logs in Dedicated vs Private? Can we set a shorter retention period for PHI traffic?
2) KMS: you mentioned BYOK for Private — can you confirm which providers are supported and whether we can integrate with our HSM cluster?
3) Draft BAA: can you highlight the difference vs. your standard BAA for Hosted customers? Specifically, we need to understand obligations around subprocessors and data return/destruction timelines.

We’ll complete the questionnaire but it would be helpful to get the SOC evidence packet and the BAA redlines earlier in parallel.

Regards,
Diane Park
Director of IT Security | Mediflow Health
diane.park@mediflow.io

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Park <diane.park@mediflow.io>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@mediflow.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-14T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today’s HIPAA discovery call

Diane — thanks, excellent questions. Answers below, plus next steps and owners.

1) Token logging retention
- Dedicated: default 90 days for request/response logs; configurable down to 7 days at deployment time for PHI workloads.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): retention controlled by customer; Redwood will provide the logging pipeline (Kafka/S3) and we can configure retention per your policies.

2) KMS / HSM support
- Private: BYOK with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault supported. We also support HSM integration via PKCS#11 connectors (requires engineering enablement; we’ll include runbook).
- Dedicated: customer-managed keys supported for disk and snapshot encryption; platform-managed keys are available as an option.

3) Draft BAA differences
- Hosted (public) customers currently are not eligible for PHI; our hosted policy only permits de‑identified data.
- The attached BAA covers Dedicated & Private; it includes explicit subprocessors list, data return/destruction timelines (30 days for active returns, 90 days for backups), and incident notification windows (72 hours). Legal can redline — we’ll accept reasonable redlines for enterprise deals.

Owners & deliverables (internal)
- Ben Carter: SOC evidence index, network diagrams, and a short FAQ addressing the questionnaire (deliverable: security-evidence-index_Q3_2026.zip) — due today EOD.
- Evelyn Hart: coordinate legal for BAA negotiation and DocuSign routing; will monitor redlines.

Scheduling
- Diane / Samir: can you confirm availability for 2026-07-16 10:00 AM PT or propose an alternate slot? We’ll use this call to review the BAA and confirm token retention/KMS details.

Attachments included: redwood_baa_draft_20260714.pdf (BAA template), security-evidence-index_Q3_2026.zip (index & links to evidence)

Thanks — will follow up with the HubSpot record and the DocuSign envelope once legal is ready.

—Vanessa

On a related internal note (Ben/Evelyn): Ben, please attach the SOC I PDF and the compressed evidence links in the packet. Evelyn, I’ll add legal to the follow-up invite once Diane confirms a time.
